original.reason: The normalization to M=1 is unjustified without first excluding M=0. The preceding observation that adjacent values differ does not do so.

judgment.reason: The M=0 case relies on an imprecise and unsupported vertex-cover assertion; it does not clearly establish the required zero-zero adjacent pair.
It correctly handles M=0, normalizes when M>0, and derives an impossible alternating two-coloring of an odd cycle.
The proof correctly excludes B=0 using non-bipartiteness, then the threshold argument forces an impossible bipartition.
It correctly treats the zero-product case via an independent set and completes the standard threshold/odd-cycle contradiction.
